params.body:
A pure refactor of the publishing path. No behaviour change: the 21 characterization tests in `tests/Feature/VehiclePublishingTest.php` are **byte-identical to main** (`git diff origin/main -- tests/Feature/VehiclePublishingTest.php` is empty). Zero mechanical edits were needed, because every class the tests name by hand (`WebhookHelper`, `SendVehicleWebhookJob`, `OwnStockService`, `IWebhookRepository`) kept its name and its calling shape.

This closes open points **O-23** and **O-25**. O-22 and O-24 stay open.

## Where the publisher went, and why

`app/Services/VehiclePublisher.php`.

`app/Support` holds the small, self-contained collaborators: `Sale` returns an array of fields, `Outbound` reads configuration, `CarpassPending` counts rows. None of the three talks to a third party. This class does exactly that: it queues messages to partner systems and pulls advertisements off a classifieds site. That is what `app/Services` stands for here (`WhatsAppService`, `BluritService`, `RealGarantService`), so that is where it lives.

The observer decides WHAT happened; the publisher decides HOW it leaves:

| observer says | publisher does |
|---|---|
| `published($vehicle)` | ring `create` |
| `unpublished($vehicle)` | ring `delete` |
| `changed($vehicle)` | ring `update` |
| `sold($vehicle)` | withdraw from the classifieds, then ring `sold` |
| `removed($vehicle)` | withdraw from the classifieds, then ring `delete` |

`changed()` is the fifth: the observer also fires an `update` on an ordinary save, and the point of the seam is that the strings `create`/`update`/`sold`/`delete` live in one class. `listOnNederlandMobiel()` and `withdrawFromPortals()` are the two Nederland Mobiel doors.

## Per moved piece: what called it before, what calls it now

| Moved | Called before | Called now |
|---|---|---|
| `VehicleObserver::triggerWebhook` (private) | `created`, `updated` x3, `deleted` | gone; the same five call sites call `VehiclePublisher::published/unpublished/changed/sold/removed`, and the identical guard (`is_complete` and the flag-or-delete-or-sold rule) is `VehiclePublisher::ring` |
| `VehicleObserver::removeFromPortals` (private) | the sold path, `deleted` | `VehiclePublisher::withdrawFromPortals`, called from `sold()` and `removed()` — same order, same two conditions (seal, then `is_on_nederland_mobiel`) |
| `VehicleObserver::magNaarBuiten` (private) | wrapped `Outbound::impact` in four places | gone; `Outbound::impact('nederlandmobiel')` is now asked in `VehiclePublisher`, `Outbound::impact('webhooks')` in `WebhookHelper` |
| `WebhookHelper::dispatchVehicleWebhookJobs` | observer (via the facade), and the test directly | kept, same signature; it is now a one-line call into `sendVehicleWebhooks(..., queued: true)`. Called by `VehiclePublisher::ring` and, unchanged, by the test |
| `WebhookHelper::triggerVehicleWebhook` | `stocklist:forceUpdateWebhook` (7 call sites), and the test directly | kept, same signature; `sendVehicleWebhooks(..., queued: false)`. The console command is untouched — it genuinely needs to run inline, it walks a whole fleet and does not want to fill a queue |
| the send-and-log block (written out twice) | inline in `triggerVehicleWebhook`, and again in `SendVehicleWebhookJob::handle` | once, in `WebhookHelper::deliver`. The job now resolves the vehicle and hands it to `deliver` |
| `OwnStockController::removeFromNederlandMobiel` body | route `ownvehicle.index.removeFromNederlandMobiel`, `VehicleObserver::updated`, `Vehicle::booted` | `OwnStockService::removeFromNederlandMobiel($vehicle)` (takes a `Vehicle` or an id). The controller method stays as the door for the route: `base64_decode` and delegate. The observer and `Vehicle::booted` call the publisher and no longer build a base64 id for a controller |

Nothing else dispatches `SendVehicleWebhookJob` and nothing else calls the two helper methods; I grepped the tree.

## No path gained or lost a webhook

- `created`: a vehicle created complete and already flagged still sends `create` from `created`, not from `updated`. `VehicleObserver::created` calls `published()`, and `ring()` lets it through because `is_complete` and `send_to_modix` are both true. Pinned by `test_a_vehicle_created_with_the_flag_on_dispatches_create_immediately`.
- `$force` in `getDealerIdForVehicleWebhook`: untouched, still private, still reached the same way. Both public entries pass `$force` straight through to `sendVehicleWebhooks`, which passes it on. `VehiclePublisher::ring` always passes `true`, exactly as `triggerWebhook` did. Pinned by `test_force_takes_the_dealer_from_the_vehicle_instead_of_the_session`, which also calls the helper with `false` and expects nothing.
- `resolveWebhookType`: unchanged, still public, still called once per receiver, now from `deliver` for both shapes (it was already called per receiver in both).
- The delete/sold exception (they leave without the flag) is copied character for character into `ring()`.
- The sold path still calls the withdrawal before the doorbell, and the observer still writes `send_to_modix = 0` with a quiet save afterwards.

## The seal: one question per service

`webhooks` was asked three times (observer before queueing, again in `SendVehicleWebhookJob::handle`, and in the inline path after the payload was already built). It is now asked once, in `WebhookHelper::sendVehicleWebhooks`, **before the fork** — which is where the two shapes cross. That placement is what keeps both pinned tests true: with the seal closed nothing is queued (`Queue::assertNothingPushed`) and nothing is sent inline (no HTTP, no `webhook_logs` row).

The one consequence worth naming: `SendVehicleWebhookJob::handle` no longer asks. A job can only exist if the seal was open at the moment it was queued, and there is exactly one place that queues one. `Outbound::allowUrl()` still runs per call in `deliver`, so the URL block still gets its per-call exception.

`nederlandmobiel` was asked in the observer in three places; it is now asked in `VehiclePublisher` (`listOnNederlandMobiel`, `withdrawFromPortals`). It stays outside `OwnStockService::sendToNederlandMobiel`, because `test_with_the_seal_closed_no_webhook_and_no_nederland_mobiel_leaves` spies on that service and requires the call not to happen at all. The last door in `executeNederlandMobielRequest` (raw cURL, invisible to the HTTP block) is untouched.

Two asymmetries I deliberately did NOT straighten, because both are behaviour and not shape:

1. `VehicleObserver::updated` withdraws from Nederland Mobiel without asking the seal first (the branch for "the dealer switched the link off"). It reaches `withdrawFromNederlandMobiel`, which does not ask either. Nothing leaves — the socket is sealed — but the local bookkeeping does run, and adding a guard would stop that. It stays as it is; the method carries a docblock saying why.
2. The observer passes `$dealer->id` to `sendToNederlandMobiel` from `created` and `$vehicle->id` from `updated`. That difference predates this PR. The publisher takes the key from the caller so the difference survives untouched, with a comment saying it is a question about behaviour.

## Not in scope, on purpose

- **`send_to_modix` is not renamed.** The column is part of the partner API contract (`VehicleApiController` returns the field), so renaming it breaks Hexon and the other receivers. Internal method names now read better (`published`, `unpublished`); the column and the API field stay exactly as they are. O-22 stays open.
- **X-98** (`ApiHelper::encrypt` is `(value * 3) + 5`) and **X-99** (a 4xx/5xx answer is not treated as a failure) are untouched and still recorded. X-99's code column now points at `WebhookHelper::deliver`, since the block it named moved there.
- **O-24** (the `deleted_at` trap on `webhooks`) is untouched; its tripwire test still stands.
- **Coalescing is not started.** It is recorded as **X-100**: four days of the live log carry 415 messages to Doorlinken Voorraad of which 189 are unique — 54% repeats, one vehicle got the same `update` twelve times, concentrated on a single dealer. Root cause is not X-97: every save that makes `is_vehicle_changed` true sends an `update`. That is a behaviour change and gets its own PR with its own test.

## Documentation

Chapter S2-10 changed only where a rule named a class or a method that moved (R S2-10.1, .2, .3, .4, .5, .10), plus one paragraph saying who says what and who says how. The rules themselves are word for word the same, because the behaviour is. O-23 and O-25 are marked done in place with what was built; X-100 is new. `92-testdekking.md` came back unchanged from `bin/rules-coverage --write` (the aggregate did not move: S2-10.10 already had a test), and `docs/bedrijfsregels.html` is regenerated with `bin/rules-page`.

## Tests

Three new tests in `tests/Feature/VehiclePublisherTest.php`, tagged `@rule S2-10.10`, covering the one moved piece that `VehiclePublishingTest` does not walk past: the Nederland Mobiel withdrawal stops at a closed seal, runs at an open one, and the route still reaches the service through the thin controller method.

Verified with `php artisan test --filter='VehiclePublishing|Webhook|Observer|Vehicle|Outbound|Sale|RulesCoverage'` (16 passed, 185 warnings, 812 assertions) and then the full suite: **709 tests, 1 failed, 61 passed, 647 warnings, 2929 assertions**. The one failure is `BuildStampTest`, which reads `.git` as a directory and cannot in a worktree; the warnings are the same worktree artifact on every test. Same run on `origin/main` in the same worktree fails the same way.
params.title: A seam for publishing: the observer says what, the publisher says how
